data.body:
## rebar-debug final report — Phase 2 complete, change on Gerrit

**Gerrit change 1404** (`846b: gate on the fact of a review, not its source`), patchset 2 at
`18699e3ace`. Plan review: **PASS, signed**, `certified` (`verified_at_sha 18f08d57c0`).

**Proven root cause.** `src/rebar/llm/code_review/bugfix_size_gate.py`, the `keyring is None` arm of
`classify_plan_review_attestation`. An unpinned DSSE principal returned an affirmative
`{"verdict": "mismatch"}`, which is in `FLAG_VERDICTS`, so `apply_bugfix_size_gate` set
`verdict["verdict"] = "BLOCK"`. Rejection was on the SOURCE of certification, never on whether a
plan review happened.

**Proof.** The paired fixture experiments hold everything constant except pinning: same minted,
signed, same-material op-cert reaches `certified`/accepted when the env is pinned and `mismatch`/flag
when it is not. Replication on the REAL reported case: with `.rebar/trusted_environments.yaml`
DELETED — the exact reported condition — `classify_plan_review_attestation('129e-2d88-cce2-492c')`
now returns `stale-head` -> `accepted`. Pre-fix, the identical call returned
`mismatch` ("signing environment 'ade0f2ef-…' is not pinned") -> `flag` -> BLOCK. That is Gerrit
1344's sole blocking finding, gone, and gone WITHOUT depending on the 1355 pin.

**RED->GREEN.** Oracles `test_classify_unpinned_signing_environment_is_accepted` and
`test_oversized_bug_fix_reviewed_in_an_unpinned_environment_does_not_block`, both observed FAILING
first (`mismatch` / `BLOCK`) and HELD OUT from the implementing subagent (moved out of its tree,
path declared off-limits). Mutation check: re-inserting the exact root cause returns both to RED;
restoring the fix returns them to GREEN. They assert observable return values, not private names,
so they are not change-detectors.

**The fix.** The chain is now four steps: record present -> decodable op-cert envelope -> SUBJECT
BINDING (ticket id + kind, read from the SIGNED payload) -> `compute_validity`. The
`trusted_env_keyring` lookup, the `verify_opcert` call, and `_plan_review_anchor` are gone. The
verdict vocabulary shrank to the `compute_validity` literals plus `error`; unknown literals still
fail OPEN, so the removal can never become a surprise block.

**The plan review earned two real improvements** (it BLOCKED twice before passing, correctly):
1. It caught that deleting `verify_opcert` would silently drop SUBJECT BINDING as well, since that
   was its only home — `opcert_from_record` merely decodes and `compute_validity` checks no ticket
   id. Binding is now re-asserted explicitly in this module, with two regressions
   (`test_classify_rejects_a_cert_bound_to_another_ticket`,
   `test_classify_rejects_a_cert_of_another_kind`, the latter proving a lying plaintext mirror
   loses to the signed payload). Without this, a valid cert replayed off another ticket would have
   been accepted.
2. It forced AC2's security reasoning to be written down rather than asserted, and AC4 to be
   restated to match the adopted policy instead of contradicting it. Both are now in the
   description and mirrored in `docs/plan-review-gate.md`.

**Scope & safety.** Caller sweep: `finalize.py` (signature unchanged) and `review_bot/retrigger.py`
(behaviour changes BY DESIGN — the same unsatisfiability seen from the recheck-review side — and
stays fail-closed on every non-accepted bucket, 15 tests pass). No new dependency; the fix restores
a path rather than creating capability; no pre-existing test was weakened — the two vocabulary
tests changed expectations literal-for-literal because the vocabulary itself shrank by design, and
gained a new assertion that the removed literals cannot linger in the BLOCKING bucket.

**Siblings.** Construct sweep for `trusted_env_keyring(...) is None -> affirmative reject`: two
sites total. The one fixed here, and `trusted_env.verify_required_environment`, whose only consumer
is `rebar verify-opcert` — a close-AUDIT surface gated on an explicitly CONFIGURED required
environment with its own enforcement window and grandfathering. Not a sibling: there the
environment is chosen deliberately by config, not imposed on every contributor. Parity census
(CLI / MCP / library / automated callers / dual direction): `review-code` N/A (Gerrit-only by
design), no MCP surface, library + both automated callers go through the shared core and inherit
the fix. The dual-direction slot is the finding worth recording — the claim gate and the close gate
NEVER consulted `trusted_env` (confirmed: no reference outside `attest/trusted_env.py`,
`verify_opcert.py`, `trusted_env_cmd.py`). The code-review gate was the lone outlier, so this
change moves it INTO line with rebar's other attestation consumers rather than out of it.

**Residual risk.** Accepted, with reasoning recorded under "Security reasoning" in the description
and in the docs: this criterion is now an anti-sloppiness gate, not an anti-adversary one, because
the attestation record lives on the attacker-writable tickets branch and there is no trust root for
an unpinned signer. The adversarial boundary remains `LLM-Review +1` AND `Verified +1`, both
bot-only, on a Gerrit-gated code branch. Nothing here widens who may vote.

**AC status.** AC1 met (documented in `docs/plan-review-gate.md` + the packaged
`rebar explain review` guide; demonstrated end to end on real change 1344/129e, not by inspection).
AC2 met (reasoning recorded, alternatives weighed, reversibility stated). AC3 met (the message that
named no remedy is deleted; the teaching finding names `review-plan` / `sign-review` /
`review-plan --status`). AC4 restated and met under the operator's decision.

NOT CLOSING until 1404 is `Verified +1` and merged.
